# gitmoap_repository_pipeline_components (Data Source)

List the components a repository's pipelines may reference. Returns this repository's own components together with those of every group above it; when two declare the same name, the nearest wins. A component whose providers are not installed here is listed and marked rather than hidden, and one owned by a group you cannot read is left out. Filter with `search` (name and description) or `own_scope_only`; pages hold up to 100 components (20 by default) and continue with `next_token`.

The token needs `pipeline:read`.



<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) The repository's id

### Optional

- `own_scope_only` (Boolean) Exclude components inherited from parent groups
- `search` (String) Match on name and description

### Read-Only

- `items` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items))

<a id="nestedatt--items"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items`

Read-Only:

- `body` (Attributes) What a component contains: its stage slots, parameters, steps, connections and the ports it
exposes. Drafts and published versions share this shape. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body))
- `created_at` (String)
- `created_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--created_by))
- `description` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `inherited` (Boolean) Whether the component belongs to a group above the group or repository being listed,
rather than to it.
- `latest_version` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `source_path` (String) Where the component is written in its repository: `.gitmoap/components/<name>.hcl`, or its
directory. Absent on a component a group owns.
- `unsatisfied_capabilities` (List of String) Capabilities the latest active version needs that no provider installed here supplies.
Left out when there are none.
- `updated_at` (String)
- `version_count` (Number)
- `versions` (Attributes List) Published versions, newest first. Present on a single-component read. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--versions))

<a id="nestedatt--items--body"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body`

Read-Only:

- `component_instances` (Attributes List) Other components this component uses. Always empty in a published version, where they have
already been expanded into steps. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--component_instances))
- `edges` (Attributes List) Connections between the component's own steps; both ends must be steps of this component. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--edges))
- `inputs` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--inputs))
- `nodes` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--nodes))
- `outputs` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--outputs))
- `parameters` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--parameters))
- `stage_slots` (List of String) The positions the component's steps occupy, in order. A pipeline using the component maps
each slot to one of its own stages.

<a id="nestedatt--items--body--component_instances"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.component_instances`

Read-Only:

- `component_id` (String)
- `component_ref` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `stage_map` (Map of String) Binds every slot the referenced component declares to a slot of the **containing** body.
- `version` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--items--body--edges"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.edges`

Read-Only:

- `id` (String)
- `source_node_id` (String)
- `source_port` (String)
- `target_node_id` (String)
- `target_port` (String)


<a id="nestedatt--items--body--inputs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.inputs`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `targets` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--inputs--targets))

<a id="nestedatt--items--body--inputs--targets"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.inputs.targets`

Read-Only:

- `node_id` (String)
- `port` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--items--body--nodes"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.nodes`

Read-Only:

- `node` (Attributes) A step in a stage: one use of a provider capability, with its configuration. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--nodes--node))
- `param_slots` (Attributes) Step fields whose values a component parameter supplies, each naming the parameter to take the
value from. A step's `config` reads parameters directly instead, with `{"$param": "<name>"}`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--nodes--param_slots))
- `stage_slot` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--items--body--nodes--node"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.nodes.node`

Read-Only:

- `allow_failure` (Boolean) When `true`, this node's failure (a non-zero exit or a timeout, after any
retries) is non-blocking: it does not fail the enclosing stage or the run.
The node's transitive dependents — which can never receive its output —
are skipped, while independent branches and later stages keep running. A
run whose only failures were `allow_failure` nodes finishes
`succeeded_with_warnings`.
- `approval` (Attributes) An approval gate on a step. With no `approvers`, anyone with Developer access to the repository
may decide; a list narrows the decision to the people, teams and roles it names, as they stand
when the approval is given. On a step that deploys to an environment requiring approval, the
list may only name approvers the environment also names. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--nodes--node--approval))
- `capability_id` (String)
- `changes` (List of String) Path globs that decide whether this step runs: when none of them matches a path the push
changed, the step is skipped. When absent and `service` is set, the service's own path globs
apply.
- `connection` (String)
- `cpu` (String)
- `environment` (String)
- `id` (String)
- `max_retries` (Number)
- `memory` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `resource_group` (Attributes) A resource group a step holds while it runs, so only one step naming it runs at a time. Unless
`mode` says otherwise, a step queues for the group, for as long as the pipeline's timeout
allows unless `max_wait_seconds` sets a shorter limit. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--nodes--node--resource_group))
- `retry_delay_seconds` (Number)
- `service` (String)
- `timeout_seconds` (Number)
- `variables_from` (String)
- `version` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--items--body--nodes--node--approval"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.nodes.node.approval`

Read-Only:

- `required` (Number) Distinct approvals needed, 1–10. On a gated environment the larger of this and the
environment's own count applies.


<a id="nestedatt--items--body--nodes--node--resource_group"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.nodes.node.resource_group`

Read-Only:

- `max_wait_seconds` (Number)
- `mode` (String) What happens when a run wants to deploy while another run holds the lock: `queue` (the
default) waits its turn, `skip` skips the step, and `cancel_previous` cancels the other run.
`cancel_previous` is available on environments only, not on a step's resource group.
- `name` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--items--body--nodes--param_slots"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.nodes.param_slots`

Read-Only:

- `allow_failure` (String)
- `connection` (String)
- `cpu` (String)
- `environment` (String)
- `max_retries` (String)
- `memory` (String)
- `retry_delay_seconds` (String)
- `service` (String)
- `timeout_seconds` (String)
- `variables_from` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--items--body--outputs"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.outputs`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `source` (Attributes) A port on one of the component's steps. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--body--outputs--source))

<a id="nestedatt--items--body--outputs--source"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.outputs.source`

Read-Only:

- `node_id` (String)
- `port` (String)



<a id="nestedatt--items--body--parameters"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.body.parameters`

Read-Only:

- `description` (String)
- `name` (String)
- `param_type` (String) The JSON shape a parameter's value must have.
- `required` (Boolean) Whether a pipeline using the component must supply a value. A required parameter cannot
have a default.



<a id="nestedatt--items--created_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.created_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.


<a id="nestedatt--items--versions"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.versions`

Read-Only:

- `capability_requirements` (List of String) The provider capabilities the version's steps use.
- `changelog` (String)
- `commit_sha` (String) The commit whose files it was published from.
- `contract_digest` (String) A SHA-256 fingerprint, in hex, of what a pipeline using the version must satisfy: its
parameters, its ports and the variables it reads. It changes only when that contract does.
- `depth` (Number) How many levels of components the version spans: 1 when it uses no other component.
- `expanded_node_count` (Number) How many steps the version expands into.
- `lifecycle_state` (String) Where a published version sits in its retirement.

A `deprecated` version still resolves for an exact reference and still runs, but no floating
reference selects it — which is what makes deprecating the safe way to retire one. A `sunset`
version refuses to resolve at all, exact reference included.
- `published_at` (String)
- `published_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--items--versions--published_by))
- `tag_name` (String) The tag that published it: `<name>/<version>`, or a plain `<version>`. Absent on a version
published before versions were published by tag.
- `variable_requirements` (List of String) The variables the version's steps read from the pipeline that uses it. Each must be declared
on the environment those steps run in, or on a group or repository above the pipeline, or
a run is refused when it starts.
- `version` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--items--versions--published_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `items.versions.published_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
